Scott & Selber Inc decreased its stake in Marriott International Class A (MAR) by 29.56% based on its latest 2017Q4 regulatory filing with the SEC. The institutional investor held 26,777 shares of the hotels and resorts company at the end of 2017Q4, valued at $3.63 million, down from 38,015 at the end of the previous reported quarter. Scott & Selber Inc who had been investing in Marriott International Class A for a number of months, seems to be less bullish one the $48.95 billion market cap company. The stock increased 0.17% or $0.23 during the last trading session, reaching $138.52. About 1.22M shares traded. Marriott International, Inc. (NASDAQ:MAR) has risen 45.53% since May 21, 2017 and is uptrending. It has outperformed by 33.98% the S&P500.
